instruction: I have 15 minutes before I need to leave for work, but my father hasn't eaten breakfast and refuses everything I offer. I can't stay home today. How can I handle this morning?
My mother spills drinks frequently now, and she gets embarrassed when I try to clean up or help her. I want to make meals easier without making her feel incapable.
My husband seems to understand me sometimes but other times looks confused by even simple instructions. When I repeat them louder, he gets upset. What can I change?
My mother asks every afternoon whether we're going somewhere, even after I tell her we're staying home. She becomes anxious each time. I am finding it hard to keep answering patiently.
My father refuses my help with bathing. He says it is embarrassing to have his daughter help him, but he is struggling to manage safely on his own. How can we approach this respectfully?

When I tell my husband it's time to leave the house, he sometimes starts shouting and refuses to move. If I keep trying to persuade him, it gets worse. We have an appointment we can't miss. What should I do in the moment?
My brother asked me to take over caring for our mother this weekend again. I've already cancelled my plans several times, and I feel resentful. I want to say no but feel guilty.
I had a really difficult day caring for my wife and now I don't want to speak to anyone. I feel emotionally numb. I don't need a big plan right now, but I don't know what would help.
My siblings agreed to take turns bringing meals to our father, but two weeks in, I'm still doing nearly all of it. I want to address this without starting another family argument.

My sister thinks our mother should move in with her, while I think we should look at other support options first. We keep arguing and haven't discussed what our mother actually wants. How do we move forward?

My father has been sleeping much more during the day and has stopped enjoying his usual activities. I have an appointment with his doctor tomorrow. What information should I prepare so I can explain the changes clearly?

A clinician dismissed my concerns about my husband's recent changes and I left without understanding what to watch for. I want to follow up, but I don't know how to make sure my concerns are addressed.
My mother was speaking and behaving normally this morning, but this afternoon she suddenly seems confused and is much harder to wake. I don't know whether I should wait and see or do something now.
My father has started holding onto furniture when walking around the house. He says he's fine and doesn't want me hovering. I'm worried he might fall, but I don't want to take away his independence.

My husband can still make his own tea, but it takes him much longer than it used to. I often do it for him because we're in a hurry. How can I help him maintain this ability without making our mornings impossible?
I'm trying to help my mother learn to use her phone to call family, but she gets upset whenever she presses the wrong button. She now refuses to practice. How can I make this easier?
I know my family needs more caregiving support, but we cannot afford to hire someone regularly. I work during the day and have very little help nearby. What options could I realistically explore?

Tomorrow my father has an appointment, groceries need to be bought, his laundry is piling up, and I have an important work deadline. I only have a few hours available. Help me decide what to do and what can wait.
My mother is struggling more at home. We could rearrange the house, ask relatives for help, or explore professional support. I don't know which option to try first or how to compare them.

I tried using a written daily schedule to help my husband follow his routine, but he ignores it and gets annoyed whenever I point to it. I thought it would help, but it seems to make things worse. What should I try instead?
